patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports difficulty in combing hair and reaching objects on high shelves for the past few months. Admits to a sedentary lifestyle.

Secondary_Symptoms: Decreased range of motion in shoulder

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diabetes mellitus type II, obesity, hypertension. On metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Sedentary lifestyle, predominately staying indoors and watching television.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies recent injuries or trauma to the arm or shoulder. No fever, weight loss, or other joint involvement.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with stiffness in his arm impacting daily activities.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’m a 65-year-old man, and over the past few months I’ve noticed stiffness in my arm, especially when trying to comb my hair or reach things on high shelves. My shoulder range of motion feels decreased, and my arm strength is about 4 out of 5, but I haven’t had any injury or fever.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any small, raised bumps on your skin that have a tiny indentation or a dimple in the center?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any small raised skin bumps with a central dimple. It’s mainly the stiffness in my arm and reduced shoulder range of motion when combing my hair or reaching high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you need to urinate more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed needing to urinate more often than usual. It’s mainly the arm stiffness and decreased shoulder range of motion that limit combing my hair and reaching high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or lacking your usual strength lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Generally, yes—I feel weaker than usual, especially in that affected arm, with the strength sitting around 4 out of 5. The stiffness makes it harder to lift and reach, but I haven’t had any other major body weakness.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any difficulty with dressing yourself or putting on your clothes lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, dressing has been harder—putting on shirts, especially pulling sleeves over my arm, takes more time because my shoulder range of motion is decreased and the arm feels stiff.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores appearing specifically along the veins in your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “I don’t recall any rash, bumps, or sores along the veins in my arms. It’s been mostly the stiffness and reduced shoulder range of motion affecting tasks like combing my hair and pulling sleeves on.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itchiness on your skin?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itchiness on my skin. It’s mainly the stiffness in my arm and the decreased shoulder range of motion affecting combing my hair, reaching high shelves, and dressing.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any pain or cramping in your calf muscles while walking that goes away once you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t get pain or cramping in my calf when I walk—at least not that I’ve noticed. My main issue stays in the arm, with stiffness and reduced shoulder range of motion that makes combing my hair and reaching high shelves difficult.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed if your stools have become unusually pale, light-colored, or clay-colored recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any changes in my stool color—nothing pale or clay-colored. It’s mostly the stiffness and reduced shoulder range of motion affecting combing my hair and reaching high shelves.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any weakness in your hands, such as difficulty gripping objects or a tendency to drop things more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “I wouldn’t say I’m dropping things, but my arm does feel weak and stiff, especially when lifting or raising it to comb my hair or reach high shelves. My hand gripping feels somewhat reduced compared to before, more because the shoulder and arm feel tight than because of sharp hand pain.”
